correctness.rationale: For every integer \(n\ge3\), group averaging cannot increase the convex objective \(\lVert P-J\rVert_2\) and reduces globally to \(p,q\) with \(p+2q\le1\). Every mode has exact \(2\times2\) Fourier eigenvalues; the positive first-harmonic mode forces the strictly convex lower envelope at \(q=(1-p)/2\). Its derivative vanishes exactly at the displayed \(p_*\). At those weights \(\lambda^+(t)\) decreases in \(t\), and \(\lambda^-(t)\) is bounded below by \(-\sqrt{p_*^2+(1-p_*)^2}\). The exact positive certificate is \(\mu_*^2-[p_*^2+(1-p_*)^2]=x(x+2)(2-x^2)/d^2>0\) because \(x^2\le3/2\); the zero-frequency nontrivial mode also lies below \(\mu_*\). This is a proof for every permitted order and every feasible chain, not extrapolation from 233 computed spectra.

The wheel source differs structurally (one universal hub versus n separate leaves). Both generic algorithmic solvability and the published cycle asymptotics fall short of this parameter law. Targeted alias and indexed searches gave no exact matching theorem, with residual unindexed risk recorded.

value.rationale: The cycle corona with one leaf per rim site is a standard natural graph family for local reversible transport. The theorem solves the full SLEM optimization for every graph order with explicit edge laws, proves rim holding probability saturates zero, pendant exchange scales as \(n^{-1}\), and determines the exact asymptotic gap \(\pi^2/n^2\), half the bare-cycle asymptotic. The new optimizing law and sharp factor-two penalty answer a meaningful network-design question, rather than arbitrary finite enumeration.
